questions.question_text: Who is responsible for the safekeeping of earnest money in a Utah transaction?
distractors: The sales agent who collected it
The title company at all times
The buyer until closing
questions.explanation: The principal broker is personally responsible for deposits held in the brokerage trust account (R162-2f-401c(1)(i)(ii)), and R162-2f-401c(1)(h) sets the deposit deadline.

questions.question_text: A transaction falls through and both the buyer and seller claim the earnest money. The broker should:
questions.correct_answer: Hold the funds until written agreement or court order
distractors: Split the funds equally between parties
Return the funds to the buyer automatically
Release the funds to whoever asks first
questions.explanation: Disputed trust money has its own rule (R162-2f-403a(8)): the broker may interplead the funds in court, or within 15 days of written notice that both parties claim them refer the parties to mediation if no suit has been filed and the contract requires mediation. R162-2f-401c(1)(e) also bars the broker from retaining any part of the deposit without both parties' written consent.

questions.question_text: Both parties in a failed transaction refuse to agree on earnest money distribution. The broker may:
questions.correct_answer: Interplead the funds with the court
distractors: Keep the funds as a brokerage fee
Release them to the seller by default
Donate them to the Recovery Fund
questions.explanation: Interpleader is allowed (R162-2f-403a(8)(a)), after which the broker disburses on the losing party's written authorization or by court order. The alternative under R162-2f-403a(8)(b) is a referral to mediation within 15 days if the contract provides for it and no suit has been filed.

questions.question_text: Absent a contrary term in the contract, how quickly must a Utah principal broker deposit a buyer's earnest money?
questions.correct_answer: Within three business days of receiving it
distractors: Within 24 hours
Within five banking days
Whenever the contract says; there is no default deadline
questions.explanation: Client money must reach a trust account within three business days of receipt (R162-2f-401c(1)(h)(i)). The contract can change that — for example by providing that funds are held for a set period or deposited on the seller's acceptance — and the parties may agree in writing to hold the money at a title company instead.

questions.question_text: A sales agent holds an earnest money check in their desk for a week before giving it to the principal broker. This is:
questions.correct_answer: A violation of prompt deposit requirements
distractors: Acceptable if the amount is under $5,000
Standard practice for new agents
Permitted until the inspection period ends
questions.explanation: A licensee must inform the principal broker promptly of funds received (R162-2f-401a(15)), and the broker then has only three business days from receipt to deposit them (R162-2f-401c(1)(h)). A week in a desk drawer defeats both.

distractors: Set by the Division of Real Estate
Fixed at 6% for residential properties
Determined by the Real Estate Commission
questions.explanation: No Utah statute or rule sets commission rates; they are negotiated between the client and the principal broker in the brokerage agreement (61-2f-308).

questions.question_text: A sales agent closes a deal and expects to receive their commission. Who pays the agent?
distractors: The seller directly at closing
The buyer through the title company
The Division from the Recovery Fund
questions.explanation: An associate broker or sales agent may not accept valuable consideration for licensed acts from anyone other than the principal broker with whom they are affiliated (61-2f-305(1)).

questions.question_text: A principal broker fails to pay a cooperating broker the agreed commission. Who has standing to sue?
distractors: The cooperating sales agent directly
The buyer who paid the commission
The Division on behalf of the broker
questions.explanation: An action to recover a fee or commission may only be brought by the principal broker (61-2f-409(2)(b)). A sales agent or associate broker may sue only their own principal broker.

questions.question_text: A seller agrees to pay a 5% commission but later claims the standard rate should be 6%. The broker's commission is:
questions.correct_answer: 5% as agreed in the listing agreement
distractors: 6% as the standard rate
Whatever the Real Estate Commission sets
Subject to Division arbitration
questions.explanation: Commission is a matter of contract under the brokerage agreement (61-2f-308). Utah has no standard rate, and the Division does not arbitrate commission disputes.

questions.question_text: An associate broker wants their split paid at closing by the title company rather than by the brokerage. Under Utah law this is:
questions.correct_answer: Allowed if the principal broker gives the title agent written instructions
distractors: Prohibited in every case
Allowed only with the seller's written consent
Allowed only for principal brokers
questions.explanation: A sales agent or associate broker may be paid by a payment instrument prepared by a title insurance agent following the principal broker's written instructions (61-2f-305(2)). R162-2f-401c(1)(d) sets what those instructions must contain, including the property, the parties paid, the amounts, and a bar on anyone else altering them.

questions.question_text: A licensee pays a $500 referral fee to an unlicensed friend who sent them a client. This is:
distractors: Acceptable — a licensee may give up to $250 for an unsolicited referral
Legal if documented as a gift only
Permitted as a marketing expense
questions.explanation: Paying valuable consideration to an unlicensed person is unlawful (61-2f-401(5)), and only one narrow exception exists: a gift of $250 or less for an unsolicited referral that results in a transaction (R162-2f-401b(1)(l)). A $500 payment exceeds it.

questions.question_text: A buyer's agent also receives a referral fee from the seller's agent for bringing a buyer. What must occur?
questions.correct_answer: Both parties must be informed of the dual compensation
distractors: Nothing; referral fees are private matters
The Division must approve the payment
The fee must be deposited in the trust account
questions.explanation: Any compensation beyond the real estate commission must be disclosed in writing to each party and paid to the licensee's principal broker (R162-2f-401a(16)). 61-2f-401(2) separately bars acting for more than one party without informed written consent.

questions.question_text: An agent who owns rental property wants to list their own property for sale. They must disclose:
questions.correct_answer: Their personal interest in the transaction
distractors: Only the fact that they hold a license
Nothing beyond what sellers normally disclose
The property's rental income history only
questions.explanation: A licensee acting as a principal must disclose their license status on initial contact (R162-2f-401a(5)), and must disclose the principal position in writing before a binding agreement (401a(6)). R162-2f-401h(3) also governs 'owner-agent' advertising, and R162-2f-401b(1)(o) bars limited agency where the licensee is a principal.

questions.question_text: A sales agent refers a client to another brokerage in a different city and receives a referral fee. This is:
questions.correct_answer: Permitted since both parties are licensed
distractors: Prohibited for out-of-state referrals
Only allowed with Division approval
Illegal if the fee exceeds $1,000
questions.explanation: Valuable consideration may expressly be shared with a principal broker of another jurisdiction (61-2f-401(5)(a)). The payment moves broker to broker, not agent to agent.

questions.question_text: Which statement about Utah compensation disclosure is correct?
questions.correct_answer: All sources of compensation must be disclosed
distractors: Only buyer compensation must be disclosed
Disclosure is optional for co-op commissions
Compensation details are confidential
questions.explanation: Any compensation in addition to the commission must be disclosed in writing to every party (R162-2f-401a(16)), and acting for more than one party requires informed written consent (61-2f-401(2)).
